body:
Review pass 33. MEASURED RESULT: the scale gate has exceeded its own 30-minute limit.

  fixture ready      11:36:52
  observed           12:10:32
  measured elapsed   33 min 40 s     against the 30-minute gate -> EXCEEDED, still running
  worker CPU         27 min 16 s
  worker RSS         2.04 GiB and falling   against 4 GiB -> never approached

The runner starts measuring at the fixture-ready signal (run-crossnobis-scale-gate.R:53), so analysis_seconds is already past 1800 and runtime_pass will be FALSE.

TWO THINGS THIS SETTLES.

First, dense local shrinkage at whole-brain scale is RUNTIME-bound, not memory-bound. Peak RSS was ~2.4 GiB against a 4 GiB budget and has fallen steadily under gc. Every memory-side concern on this epic - including my own earlier projections about packed width and the 4 GiB crossover - was aimed at the wrong constraint. The binding cost is per-support k-by-k solve work across 52416 nodes and six edges.

Second, it fails in the MOST FAVOURABLE configuration available: q=2, three partitions, six edges, local covariance singular for 84% of supports. There is no cheaper statistically-shaped workload for this path, and both fixes for the degeneracy multiply the dominant cost 5-6x - so a meaningful fixture sits further outside the gate, not nearer it.

CONCLUSION, already named in your acceptance: "If dense local shrinkage misses the gate, version 0.1 supports brain-scale diagonal metrics and explicitly scopes dense metrics to smaller supports/node sets."

Recommend Epic 8 close by recording:
  - brain-scale diagonal / identity metrics SUPPORTED - same 52k voxel volume, 166 s end to end
  - dense local metrics at whole-brain node counts NOT SUPPORTED in 0.1 - exceeds 30 minutes
  - a declared dense-metric ceiling stated in node count and support size, found by re-running the
    gate at reduced node counts until it fits

That is a real 0.1 scope statement and a stronger result than a pass would have been. It is precisely what this epic set out to establish, and the package comes out of it with an honest boundary rather than an untested promise.
